literal.prompt: В каком направлении вены несут кровь?

literalGroups.primaryGround: The NHLBI definition directly says veins bring blood to the heart and arteries take blood away. Venae cavae and pulmonary veins are concrete examples; only the heartward direction answers the general question. All four options are short directional phrases, with one key.

literalGroups.literal: Вены несут кровь к сердцу. Верхняя и нижняя полые вены приносят кровь из тела в правое предсердие, а лёгочные вены — из лёгких в левое.
literalGroups.primaryGround: The first sentence states the main directional fact. The second gives the superior/inferior vena cava route to the right atrium and pulmonary vein route from the lungs, preserving the distinction that vein direction is defined relative to the heart rather than oxygen content.

literalGroups.literal: Артерии уносят кровь от сердца; аорта направляет её к органам тела.
literalGroups.primaryGround: NHLBI defines arteries as taking blood away from the heart and states that the aorta carries blood from the heart to the rest of the body.

literalGroups.literal: Верхняя и нижняя полые вены приносят кровь из тела в правое предсердие.
literalGroups.primaryGround: NHLBI states that the superior and inferior vena cava bring oxygen-poor blood from the body to the right atrium; this is a concrete route fact beyond the prompt/key.

literalGroups.literal: К лёгким кровь отводит лёгочная артерия, выходящая из сердца.
literalGroups.primaryGround: NHLBI says the pulmonary artery takes blood from the heart to the lungs; the option is a destination reached by a pulmonary artery, not the general direction of veins.

literalGroups.literal: Аорта направляет кровь из сердца к остальным тканям организма.
literalGroups.primaryGround: NHLBI says the aorta carries blood leaving the heart to the rest of the body; this gives a concrete arterial route for the destination distractor.
